decisions.rationale: Keep the frozen topic order. Separate true prerequisites from later enrichment and remove any the objective does not need (for example Flyway before introductory JPA). Make each early Fast use self-contained: at FT4, teach and check only the MockMvc behavior available before @MockitoBean/ProblemDetail, or add a minimum just-in-time bridge; at FT3, bridge only the relationship concepts the skim needs and move checks that depend on FT4/FT6 later. The 'track-order prerequisite gate' is implemented as an explicit per-Fast-day prerequisite table in intake.md that the critics can verify, not as new tooling (tooling is out of scope for a course intake).

Keep the syllabus and project rows. Standard S6: the three S6 instructional pages and their checks come before the Build block. Fast FT5/FT7: an explicit pre-implementation teach-and-diagnostic phase precedes project work, and the build is used for transfer and feedback. Embedded reminders may stay but never count as prior teaching.

Accepted as delivery-plan precision, without new tooling or schema. Following the Python/Web/React intake precedent, intake.md records a structured increment table for FT1-FT4, FT6 and FT8 covering: calendar rows referenced (unchanged), extension order, named public tests, claimed vs practised fragments, and the minute plan inside each 70-minute block. A machine-readable package/overlay manifest and its lock/schema/check binding belong to the track-overlay task (pep-t1-track-overlays), which owns Fast overlays for every course; they are not added in this intake.

Do not add or rename a topic. Narrow o1 to identifying a small, explicitly named set of common risks relevant to this course's API; keep o2/o3 on diagnosing and mitigating those risks. The full OWASP Top 10 stays optional reference.

Keep the frozen 45-minute Standard block and MCQ/coding formats. Reserve explicit transition and test-run time by reducing the item count or simplifying the coding task scope as needed. A full-route pilot is a module-authoring step, recorded as an open item. Fast timing stays open.

Remove the parenthetical Task 1/Task 2 prompts from the blueprint, and the task-specific sections and expected outcomes from intake.md. Keep only objective references, format assignment, item counts, the Standard 45-minute schedule, toolchain/environment requirements and the open Fast timing. Assessment tasks, tests, keys, rubrics and solutions stay out of the repository.

Inside the fixed FT5 block, add a short embedded teach-then-check before the WARN logging action, funded from apply or wrap minutes. If it does not fit, remove the logging action and leave logging to the skim/reference. No calendar change.

Make visibility explicit: read the aggregate status first, then configure component visibility with an exposure/security caveat before reading the database contributor. Do not imply that component details are shown by default.
Separate the mechanisms in o2: curated dependency management through the Boot BOM/parent, convenient dependency sets through starters, plus auto-configuration and the embedded server.

Use a shell-neutral, unquoted Surefire selector (for example mvn -q -o test -Dtest=increment<N>.*), to be proven against the authored package layout at module time. Keep mvn -q -o test as the single cumulative command. Record a Windows command-line smoke run as a module-authoring release check.

Same decision as spring-intake-edu-003. intake.md binds all six increments and their public-test names to one course-level project in a structured table. Repository-native package representation and lock/schema/check binding are deferred to pep-t1-track-overlays as a cross-course item; no tooling or schema change in this intake.

For sources whose fetched bytes include dynamic or challenge content, also record a hash of a deterministic extraction of the relevant section and the canonicalization method, keeping the URL and retrieval time. Prefer versioned docs URLs (for example the 4.1.1 reference) where available.
